title: Federal conditions for a pharmacist's dispensing of a nonprescription controlled substance at retail without a prescription
subtopic: Controlled substances dispensed at retail without a prescription
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1306.26, a controlled substance listed in Schedules II, III, IV, or V which is not a prescription drug as determined under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act may be dispensed by a pharmacist without a prescription to a purchaser at retail, provided that: (a) such dispensing is made only by a pharmacist, as defined in part 1300, and not by a nonpharmacist employee even if under the supervision of a pharmacist, although after the pharmacist has fulfilled his professional and legal responsibilities set forth in the section the actual cash, credit transaction, or delivery may be completed by a nonpharmacist; (b) not more than 240 cc. (8 ounces) of any such controlled substance containing opium, nor more than 120 cc. (4 ounces) of any other such controlled substance, nor more than 48 dosage units of any such controlled substance containing opium, nor more than 24 dosage units of any other such controlled substance may be dispensed at retail to the same purchaser in any given 48-hour period; (c) the purchaser is at least 18 years of age; (d) the pharmacist requires every purchaser of a controlled substance under the section not known to him to furnish suitable identification (including proof of age where appropriate); (e) a bound record book for dispensing of controlled substances under the section is maintained by the pharmacist, containing the name and address of the purchaser, the name and quantity of controlled substance purchased, the date of each purchase, and the name or initials of the pharmacist who dispensed the substance to the purchaser, and the book is maintained in accordance with the recordkeeping requirement of 21 CFR 1304.04; and (f) a prescription is not required for distribution or dispensing of the substance pursuant to any other Federal, State or local law. Under 1306.26(g), central fill pharmacies may not dispense controlled substances to a purchaser at retail pursuant to the section. 21 CFR 1300.01 defines pharmacist as any pharmacist licensed by a State to dispense controlled substances, including any other person (e.g., pharmacist intern) authorized by a State to dispense controlled substances under the supervision of a pharmacist licensed by such State.
exam_relevance: Tests the federal conditions on a nonprescription controlled-substance sale - pharmacist dispensing, the 48-hour volume and dosage-unit caps, age 18, identification of purchasers not known to the pharmacist and the bound record book - and that the route is closed where any other Federal, State or local law requires a prescription and to a central fill pharmacy.

exceptions: After the pharmacist has fulfilled the pharmacist's professional and legal responsibilities under 21 CFR 1306.26, the actual cash, credit transaction, or delivery may be completed by a nonpharmacist.
common_confusions: The federal route depends on no other Federal, State or local law requiring a prescription for the substance; it does not override a State prescription requirement.
A nonpharmacist employee may not do the dispensing even under a pharmacist's supervision, although a nonpharmacist may complete the cash, credit transaction or delivery afterwards.
The volume and dosage-unit caps run per purchaser over any given 48-hour period and are higher for a preparation containing opium.
For this section a pharmacist includes a person, such as a pharmacist intern, authorized by a State to dispense controlled substances under the supervision of a licensed pharmacist.
verification_notes: 21 CFR 1306.26 and the definition of pharmacist in 21 CFR 1300.01 read in the eCFR, current through 2026-09-14, on 2026-09-16.
